summary: Cold read of the poc-responsiveness plan draft (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only) returned NOT CONVERGED with eleven findings; all were verified against the repository and all held. The draft was not saveable at all - it lacked the frontmatter attesting the live decision corpus - and its task split violated the execution model by putting controller disconnect handling, model abort propagation and warehouse cancellation inside a task labelled frontend. Three limits the plan had left silent are now named, and the retry moved inside the provider boundary so that 'no repeated governed query' is structural rather than promised. Two findings needed the human because they changed scope: how far cancellation should go, and whether freshness - which turned out to need a whole authenticated route rather than a wire-up - stays in this story.
gaps: The draft lacked the required decisions_reviewed frontmatter attesting every active decision, not merely the subset named in prose, so plan save would refuse it outright.
Critical limits were unspecified and could not be silently defaulted: no maxTokens value, no priorTurns count or size limits, and no measurable latency threshold behind the word 'seconds'.

C3 did not bound the real payload: capping turn count and question length leaves nested selection fields unbounded, so the serialized priorTurns can still be oversized; and a server-only cap would make long normal conversations fail unless the client trims to the same named budget while retaining oldest-first order.

Cancellation was promised with no viable implementation seam: the stream controller has no disconnect signal, the LLM port accepts no abort signal, and warehouse execution uses a statement_timeout and a Promise.race that do not cancel the underlying Postgres work.

Freshness had no reachable API design: the shell cannot consume a cross-source batch minimum without a new authenticated endpoint, typed DTOs, route registration, Swagger contracts, a client fetch and cache policy and tests - none of which appeared in the approach, the surface table or any task.
The new freshness port's multi-engine behaviour was unstated across three warehouse adapters, leaving compilation and semantics to the implementer.

Surface Impact was incomplete and internally contradictory - /api/chat/stream marked Unchanged while gaining disconnect behaviour, the new freshness API absent, provenance consumers absent, and no owning task per row.

The verification plan could not falsify several claims: no named test leaves or commands, no SSE frame-split parsing tests, no backend abort proof, no explicit latency bound, no registration of new backend tests, and no D-0006 format-baseline work for the two currently excluded files.

The retry lacked a defined internal result contract: absent tool use, malformed input and mark_unsupported are collapsed to one unsupported outcome, with no named discriminant, no propagation through mocks and fakes, and no stated retry boundary relative to governed execution.
contradictions: The task split contradicted the execution model: assistant-streaming-ui was labelled frontend while owning controller disconnect handling, model abort propagation and warehouse-query cancellation, and shell-freshness-and-dock was labelled fullstack; the draft also called tasks 'independent' while the harness orders tasks sequentially.

C5 left an interaction boundary undecided: dock and Ask share one provider in the application shell, so without a rule either valid dock-to-Ask transitions cancel a live request or abandoned work continues after the user leaves.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - the plan now opens with decisions_reviewed frontmatter listing all 28 IDs printed by forge decision list --active.

REPO-ANSWERED - the task decomposition is five SINGLE-RUNTIME leaves with explicit dependencies and sequential ordering: bounded-generation (backend), stream-cancel (backend), streaming-ui (frontend), freshness-api (backend), freshness-and-dock (frontend). The backend halves of cancellation and freshness are no longer hidden inside frontend tasks.

REPO-ANSWERED - the limits are named and justified: maxTokens 2048 (about 18x a real ~110-token selection and about 8 percent of the observed 24,313-token runaway; 512 and 2048 measured identically at stopReason tool_use, so the value is headroom rather than tuning); priorTurns capped at 8 entries, a 16,000-character serialized payload and 2,000 characters per question, checked BEFORE serialization so nested selection fields cannot smuggle an oversized body past a count-only cap; and the live check requires a follow-up under 5 seconds. The client trims to the same named budget so long conversations degrade rather than fail, with oldest-first order preserved because chat.service.ts:153 reads priorTurns.at(-1) as the latest turn.

REPO-ANSWERED - the retry result gains an explicit no_tool_block discriminant distinct from unsupported, carried through the LlmProvider port and its mock and fake implementations, and the retry executes INSIDE the provider boundary before chat.service reaches execution, which makes 'no repeated governed query' structural rather than promised.

REPO-ANSWERED - the freshness port is implemented for Postgres and returns a deliberate typed unavailable on starrocks.adapter.ts and starrocks-mysql.adapter.ts, so all three compile and none invents a value.

REPO-ANSWERED - Surface Impact is rewritten with an owning task per row, /api/chat/stream reclassified as Changed, and the new freshness route, the warehouse port, provenance dataAsOf, the D-0006 files and the test-registration files all listed. The verify plan names concrete leaves and files, adds SSE split-frame and multi-frame parsing tests, a controller abort proof, the gated DB proof with a dead-port negative control, and the 5-second live threshold.

REPO-ANSWERED - C9 makes D-0006 explicit: bedrock.provider.ts and postgres.adapter.ts are both in .prettierignore, so the tasks that edit them format them, remove the entries, and update the quality-gate baseline map in the same change - a ledgered lesson from the assistant story, where de-ignoring without formatting left format:check red.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - cancellation is BOUNDED, not total: the controller observes disconnect, stops writing frames and aborts the model call, while a query already in flight expires under the existing statement_timeout rather than being cancelled. Chosen over adding pg_cancel_backend on a side connection, and over dropping cancellation entirely. The limit is written into the code comment and the task contract so it is not later rediscovered as a bug, and expected aborts are handled silently rather than recorded as backend_error. Dock collapse and dock-to-Ask navigation do NOT cancel, because one AskProvider holds one thread; leaving the assistant area does.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - freshness stays in this story as its OWN backend task with the authenticated route, typed DTOs under decision 0019, allow-list registration, Swagger contracts and the gated DB proof, sequenced after the latency and streaming work so the reported fix ships first. Chosen over removing the dead pill and deferring the real endpoint.
open_items: The roadmap item's acceptance criteria predate the diagnosis and still name cap-and-retry as the remedy for slowness; roadmap criteria are write-once (fill refuses to overwrite a non-blank field, heal takes no arguments), so the confirmed spec and this plan are authoritative and the plan says so in Risks.

docs/specs/assistant-and-exploration.md remains a draft after being amended to mark its pre-build paragraph DELIVERED; it needs its own spec grill to be re-confirmed. The shipped assistant story's evidence is unaffected.

Carried, non-blocking: no 3F location is recorded in docs/, so ap-south-1 rests on the code default plus decision 0003's India-residency line; 0027 should be amended if a real residency requirement exists.
Accepted limit, recorded so it is not mistaken for a defect: an abandoned question's warehouse query is bounded by statement_timeout, not cancelled.

rounds.question: **How far should cancellation go?** The grill found I promised it without a viable seam. Today: the stream controller observes no client disconnect, the LLM port takes no abort signal, and warehouse queries are bounded by Postgres `statement_timeout` (`postgres.adapter.ts:90`, error 57014) plus a `Promise.race` — a timeout, not a cancellation. Truly stopping an in-flight query means issuing `pg_cancel_backend` from a second connection, which is real design work for a polish story.
options: Bounded: stop the model call and the stream, let the query expire (Recommended)
Full: also cancel the Postgres query
rounds.chosen: Bounded: stop the model call and the stream, let the query expire (Recommended)

rounds.question: **Freshness is now a whole endpoint, not a wire-up.** The grill found the shell cannot consume a cross-source batch minimum without a new authenticated route with typed DTOs, Swagger contracts, allow-list registration, a client fetch/cache policy and tests — and the freshness port would need implementing or deliberately stubbing across **three** warehouse adapters (postgres, starrocks, starrocks-mysql). Plus `postgres.adapter.ts` is in `.prettierignore`, so D-0006 formatting comes with it. That is a bigger task than the latency fix you actually reported.
options: Keep it, as its own task (Recommended)
Just remove the dead pill now, defer real freshness
Keep it, and accept the story is four to five tasks
rounds.chosen: Keep it, as its own task (Recommended)

rounds.question: Closing the plan grill. Eleven findings, all verified and folded in. The substantive ones: the plan wasn't saveable without frontmatter attesting all **28** active decisions; my task split put controller disconnect and query cancellation inside a task labelled *frontend*, so it's now **five single-runtime leaves** with explicit dependencies; and three limits I'd left silent are now named — `maxTokens: 2048`, `priorTurns` capped at 8 entries / 16,000 serialized chars / 2,000 chars per question, and a follow-up under **5s** in the live check. The retry moved **inside the provider boundary** so "no repeated governed query" is structural rather than promised, with a `no_tool_block` discriminant so it can't retry a genuine refusal. Your two calls are in: cancellation is bounded (model and stream stop; an in-flight query expires under `statement_timeout`, and the code says so), and freshness is its own backend task with the route, DTOs, allow-list and a deliberate *unavailable* on both starrocks adapters. D-0006 formatting for the two prettier-ignored files is now an explicit criterion rather than a surprise.
options: Record the pass and board it (Recommended)
rounds.chosen: Record the pass and board it (Recommended)
